explanation: Human blood is always red: bright red when rich in oxygen and darker red when it carries less. Veins look blue because of the way skin scatters and absorbs light.

claims.text: The blood inside human veins is not blue: human blood is always red.
Oxygen-rich blood is bright red and oxygen-poor blood is a darker red.
Veins look blue because of how skin and tissue scatter and absorb different colours of light.
